newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares slide as European bourses fall.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares slide as European bourses fall.

text.p: Norwegian shares fell heavily on Wednesday taking a lead from jittery European bourses and a slide in debt markets.

"There was nothing exceptional in today's market. We simple followed the rest of Europe down. Bonds were weak because of the fall in U.S. Treasuries in Asia and that help to push us lower," said one broker.

Oslo's Total share index slid 1.8 percent, or almost 17 points, to end at 933.08 points. A weak opening on Wall Street sent the index to an intra-day low at 930.80 points, before it clawed back a few points ahead of the close.
The decline did little to depress trade and turnover amounted to a healthy 974 million crowns.
Real estate company Steen & Strom accounted for 195 million crowns of the day's total trade after its third largest shareholder sold out to the largest shareholder.
The sale did little to depress the price, which closed three crowns up at 82 crowns.
Of the blue chips Norsk Hydro was the most heavily traded at 157 million crowns, although the volatile stock fell six crowns to 328 crowns.
